title: Enterprise integrations and capability limits
bodyMarkdown:
## Plan a supported enterprise integration

1. Identify the workload, tenant and desired identity/lifecycle feature. Separate user identity, workload/provider authentication, directory metadata, posture and secret access; none independently grants a secret.
2. Check the exact selected interface/provider/profile implementation and qualification. A canonical v1 requirement, schema field or synthetic integration form is not a connected capability.
3. Choose the existing trusted issuer, audience, registered client, scoped grants and freshness/expiry policy. Enterprise locks and signed administration cannot be weakened by an include or personal preference.
4. Keep corporate and personal configuration read/resolve/validate/save client-side through their approved network and credentials. Honor file permissions, VPN and CORS limits; use an explicit native integration where supported instead of a hosted fetch proxy.
5. Prepare synthetic allowed/denied, cross-tenant, stale/revoked and uncertain-outcome tests at each actual interface. Bind required audit and recovery ownership before real enrollment. No new IdP/KMS/helpdesk purchase or provider account follows from this guide.

## Preview an integration without connecting it

In the local Integrations collection, open create/edit for synthetic metadata, review the selected type/configuration fields, and inspect saved/error/retry states. Cancel a deletion before testing an explicitly confirmed synthetic deletion. Identity/provider controls in Settings remain demo settings: selecting an issuer does not authenticate, connect or widen permissions.

## Keep audit separate from telemetry

Required audit records the verified actor/authority, exact operation/policy/outcome and approved provenance under a durable versioned contract. OTLP supports operational trends but does not prove immutable retention or exactly-once delivery. A required audit failure denies the protected effect. Raw bodies, secret-derived hashes, bearer/DPoP material and decrypted configuration do not belong in logs, help or search.

Hosted first-run association provisioning is a bounded separate contract, not enterprise configuration orchestration. Authentication and association creation do not authorize local key import/export, arbitrary mappings, a charge or stronger unavailable custody. Resolve supported opt-outs/locks before hosted network using actual documented interface capabilities, without guessing flags.
capabilityStatus: Enterprise identity, lifecycle, audit and hosted features need their selected interface and qualified deployment capabilities. Browser integration and issuer settings are demonstrations, not live connections or permissions.
